chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about a man who freed his female slave upon his death, so he said: 'Her waiting period is the waiting period of a free woman whose husband has died, four months and ten days.'

He said: And I asked him about a man who freed his female slave while he was alive, and he had been having intercourse with her, so he said: 'Her waiting period is the waiting period of a free woman who has been divorced, three menstrual periods.'
As for that which indicates that the manumission mentioned in these narrations, when it is after death, [is the intended meaning], is what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a freed female slave after her master's death or divorce?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the legal status of a *Umm al-Walad* (mother of a child) upon manumission, establishing that her waiting period (*Iddah*) aligns with that of a free woman based on the nature of the emancipation. When manumission occurs posthumously, she observes the widow's *Iddah* of four months and ten days; if manumitted during life after cohabitation, she observes the divorcee's *Iddah* of three menstrual cycles. This distinction highlights the Shia juristic principle that manumission elevates the slave's legal standing to that of a free woman for ritual and familial purposes.
